title: hmac_auth plugin config
description: The `config` object of an enabled `hmac_auth` plugin, generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3), component HmacAuthConfig and every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. This is Edge's own configuration schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md); the plugin catalog records when Edge requires it.

HmacAuthConfig.description: Plugin: hmac_auth — versioned HMAC request authentication with mandatory request-body integrity protection. The Ferrum profiles (`ferrum-hmac-v2`) uses `Authorization: hmac` and a Ferrum signing base; the `rfc9421` profile verifies RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signatures (`Signature-Input` / `Signature`, `hmac-sha256`, key looked up by `keyid` among the Consumers' `hmac_auth` secrets). RFC 9530 defines Content-Digest. Requests must include exactly one of Digest or Content-Digest matching the original body (`rfc9421` requires Content-Digest and must cover it). Sending both headers is refused as ambiguous; unsupported algorithms and malformed members fail closed. The signing base's FIRST field is the profile version, so a signature produced under one profile can never verify under another. `ferrum-hmac-v2` (the default) signs the profile version, matched proxy namespace, credential identity, normalized authority, method, raw path, raw query, Date, literal digest value, and a mandatory client nonce, and makes each accepted request single-use by claiming that nonce against a declared replay authority before backend dispatch. A verbatim transport retry is therefore a replay and is rejected; safe retries send a fresh nonce with a recomputed signature. HBONE CONNECT and request-body-transformer compositions fail closed. The pre-authentication body path is bounded by max_body_bytes (default 10 MiB). A WebSocket handshake (HTTP/1.1 Upgrade, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 Extended CONNECT) is signed over the EMPTY body: tunnel DATA is never drained as a request body, so the transport proves the handshake's empty representation from its own wire framing, and a handshake that declares a body is rejected.

clock_skew_seconds.description: Maximum allowed clock skew in seconds for the Date header freshness window. Bounded because the fixed replay retention horizon (601s) is derived from twice this ceiling, so no reload can shorten an already-admitted request's protection.

signing_profile.description: Versioned signing profile. 'ferrum-hmac-v2' requires a client nonce in the Authorization parameters, binds it into the signature, and makes each signed request single-use. 'rfc9421' verifies (never signs) exactly one RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signature with alg 'hmac-sha256' (an absent alg means hmac-sha256; any other is refused). Covered components must include @method, @authority, @path, @query, content-digest, every signed_headers entry, and every required_components entry; 'created', 'keyid', and 'nonce' are required, 'expires' is enforced when sent, 'created' must be within clock_skew_seconds, and the nonce is claimed single-use like v2 (in its own replay domain). Unknown algorithms, components, component parameters, and signature parameters are refused. Supported derived components are @method (the wire method: CONNECT for an HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 WebSocket Extended CONNECT), @authority, @path, @query, and @request-target (the target as sent, including HTTP/1.1 absolute form and an empty query).

replay_scope.description: Required for every profile; there is no default. Use 'shared' together with sync_mode 'redis' for any deployment running more than one gateway replica: every replica then claims each nonce through one atomic Redis SET NX EX. Use 'process' to declare a single-process deployment whose replay protection is stable across equivalent reloads but explicitly not cross-replica. There is no fallback between them — a shared-backend timeout, partition, authentication failure, or capacity failure rejects the request instead of falling back to freshness-only acceptance.

replay_max_entries.description: Capacity this process-scoped authority enforces against the shared replay lane (at most 10,000,000; use replay_scope 'shared' for more). At capacity only expired markers are reclaimed; if none can be, the request is refused (503) rather than a live marker evicted. Repeated full-live refusals are O(1) until an expiry is actually due, and a due reclamation pops only markers whose expiry has passed from an ordered expiry index, never rescanning live markers. An equivalent reload applies the new cap without forgetting live markers. Ignored for 'shared'.

signed_headers.description: Lowercase request header names every accepted signature must cover, for all profiles. Under the Ferrum profiles each is appended to the signing base, in this order, as one '\n{name}:{value}' line after the nonce, where value is the RFC 9421 section 2.1 canonical value (each field line trimmed, joined by ', '). Under rfc9421 each must appear in the covered components. A configured header missing from the request is refused (401). Signature carriers and connection-specific fields cannot be named. Omitted or empty leaves the signing base unchanged.

required_components.description: rfc9421 only (rejected with the Ferrum profiles): additional derived components every signature must cover beyond the mandatory @method, @authority, @path, @query, and content-digest. Require header fields with signed_headers.

max_body_bytes.description: Pre-authentication request-body ceiling in bytes (at most 256 MiB). Only a request whose signature already verified is buffered, and the stricter of this, the route, and the global request-body limits applies; a larger signed body is refused (413).

sync_mode.description: Replay-marker storage. 'redis' is required by (and only valid with) replay_scope 'shared'; it is what makes replay protection cross-replica. Any RESP-compatible single-endpoint server works (Redis Cluster is not supported and is screened, not assumed).

redis_url.description: Redis connection URL with a redis:// or rediss:// scheme and a non-empty authority/hostname. Must not carry a URL fragment; TLS skip-verify is only FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY. Required when sync_mode is 'redis'.

redis_tls.description: Enable TLS for the Redis connection. CA verification uses gateway-level FERRUM_TLS_CA_BUNDLE_PATH; skip-verify uses FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY.

redis_key_prefix.description: Key prefix for shared replay markers. Must be non-empty when supplied. Defaults to `{FERRUM_NAMESPACE}:hmac_auth:{plugin-config-id}`, which isolates independent policies inside a namespace while keeping every replica of one policy claiming against the same keyspace. An explicit prefix is the opt-in for deliberately sharing a keyspace across policies.

redis_pool_size.description: Number of multiplexed Redis connections. Must be between 1 and 128.

redis_connect_timeout_seconds.description: Redis connection timeout in seconds. Must be greater than zero.

redis_health_check_interval_seconds.description: Health check ping interval when Redis is unavailable. Must be greater than zero.
